title: Indirect Calorimetry-Guided Nutritional Support in Mechanically Ventilated Children (CALI-PED)
official: Use of Indirect Calorimetry to Guide Caloric Intake in Children on Mechanical Ventilation in the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit: A Prospective Comparative Study
summary:
Adequate nutritional support is essential in critically ill children receiving invasive mechanical ventilation. Current nutritional prescriptions are commonly based on predictive equations, which may inaccurately estimate individual energy requirements and contribute to underfeeding or overfeeding.

CALI-PED is a single-center, prospective, interventional pilot study designed to evaluate whether indirect calorimetry-guided nutritional support reduces interindividual variability in energy intake adequacy among mechanically ventilated children in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU).

Fifty children will be prospectively enrolled and compared with a historical cohort of 141 patients managed using conventional nutritional targets based on the Schofield predictive equation. In the prospective cohort, resting energy expenditure will be measured daily using indirect calorimetry, for up to seven days of invasive mechanical ventilation, and enteral caloric prescriptions will be adjusted accordingly.

The primary outcome is the interindividual variability in the ratio of actual energy intake to the reference energy target on days 2 and 3 of mechanical ventilation. Secondary outcomes include protein intake, agreement between predicted and measured energy requirements, changes in resting energy expenditure over time, duration of mechanical ventilation, PICU length of stay, and incidence of nosocomial infections.

This pilot study aims to determine whether indirect calorimetry can improve the individualization and consistency of nutritional support in critically ill children.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Children younger than 18 years of age.
* Body weight ≥10 kg.
* Invasive mechanical ventilation.
* Expected duration of invasive mechanical ventilation \>48 hours.
* Child's assent to participate, whenever feasible.
* Written informed consent obtained from at least one parent or legal guardian.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Limitation or withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment planned at the time of admission to the pediatric intensive care unit.
* Brain death.
* Requirement for a specific dietary regimen due to an underlying condition, including diabetic ketoacidosis or an inherited metabolic disorder.
* Gastrointestinal disorders interfering with enteral nutrition, including short bowel syndrome or malabsorption.
* Participation in another research study with an ongoing exclusion period.
* Concurrent participation in another interventional clinical trial that could interfere with the present study.
